subject: pol-con
title: (R)POL.CON.------SPT.DYM.
description: Diagram in SR(TRS)II-38 (Social Reality / Trans-Information, Level Two) accompanying Braxton's framing of culture-information focus: 'the collective forces which dictate how given information lines are interpreted to either the composite spectrum (people) of a given culture, or to the composite whole of its effective parameter (which in this case is planet Earth).' (C)POL-CON (the concept of political conformity) is crossed with SPT-DYM (spectacle dynamics): the question is what political-conformity produces when crossed with spectacle-dynamics — the (c) prefix marking that this is the structural design, not a particular policy. POL-P (political particulars) feeds into the subject from the upper-left. MT-INFO (multi-information) and SPT-DYM itself form the upper-right cluster. ALT-F (alternative functionalism) and LK-IMP (linkage implication) cluster on the right output. MOT-DY (motion dynamics) sits centrally. INFO-AF-B (information-affinity basis) anchors the lower-center. IF-ST-DY (information-style dynamics) hangs on the lower-right margin. Structural argument: political-conformity-as-concept crossed with spectacle-dynamics is mediated by motion-dynamics as central hub, with political-particulars as upstream and information-affinity-basis as the lower foundation. The diagram exposes Braxton's structural diagnostic: the spectacle-pull of western culture works through political-conformity precisely because motion-dynamics (the apparent activity of information) is the hub — what looks like political life is in fact motion-dynamics in the service of spectacle. Alternative-functionalism and linkage-implication remain as theoretical outputs, but they require the information-style-dynamics edge to actually manifest, and that edge is marginal to the operative configuration.
